description: One resource table for all three baselines. Same role, same limits, same runtime image where the roles are comparable. Limits are ceilings, not measured usage.
by_design_differences: B0 runs Keycloak 24.0.5; both B1 baselines run Keycloak 26.6.4 (the PQC baseline mounts a patched keycloak-services 26.6.4 jar).

B0's Keycloak (role `keycloak`) is on the repeated E-COST/E-LOAD measurement path (login and token issuance on every attempt) and keeps the heavier tier (1.5 cpu / 1536 MiB). B1's Keycloak (role `keycloak_login`) only handles the one-time F1 login, which is measured and reported separately and never pooled into repeated authorization; F2-F4 token issuance for B1 is handled by bank-issuer instead. B1's Keycloak therefore runs at the generic app tier (1.0 cpu / 1024 MiB) rather than the B0 tier, since giving it the same footprint as a component that is actually hammered on every measured attempt would not make the comparison fairer.
B1-C2 gateways are OQS nginx (hybrid post-quantum TLS); B0 and B1-C0 use nginx:alpine.
B0's TPP is a Node application; the B1 TPPs are Spring Boot.
